name: Illegal Wildlife Trade Challenge Fund Extra

funder.name: Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs (Defra)

summary: UK government grants of £600,000 to £1.5 million for two- to four-year projects that scale up approaches against illegal wildlife trade that have already worked at a smaller scale.

geography.label: IWT Challenge Fund Round 12 eligible countries

reporting: Annual and half-year progress reports, reviewed each year, against the project's objectives (outputs, ethics, environmental impact), plus a final report at the end of the award.

steps: Initial review, expert scoring and sift meeting
Expert review, sift and Defra funding decision

eligibility.rule: Applies as an organisation, not an individual; not a foreign government or its agency
Yearly request at most 25% of the lead organisation's average yearly income over the last 3 years
Scales up IWT work that has already shown success and impact at a smaller scale
Project lasts 2 to 4 years and completes by 31 August 2031
Project includes a poverty reduction focus
Not a target of UK government sanctions and not a Russian organisation
No other application for the same or a similar project this year to IWT, Darwin Plus or OCEAN
Not an application already resubmitted once, unless the project is significantly different

documents: Cover letter, 2 sides of A4 maximum

opens.quote: Applications for Round 12 opened on 30th September 2026.

administered_by.quote: NIRAS IWT Challenge Fund Administrator; first point of contact for projects and applicants.

geography.quote: Projects must primarily deliver benefits and activities in eligible countries listed in Table 4.

access.quote: All applications should be submitted via the Flexi-Grant application portal.

window.quote: Applications to IWT Challenge Fund Extra are a dual stage process

amount.quote: IWT Challenge Fund Extra grants, ranging from £600,000 to £1.5 million, are for projects aimed at expanding activities that have a primary focus on addressing IWT

reporting.quote: Projects must provide Annual and Half Year progress reports that are reviewed each year.

effort.quote: Stage 1 Application Deadline - 23:59 GMT on Monday 23rd November 2026.
Call for Stage 2 is by invitation only (application link to be provided) by mid-February 2027. Stage 2 Application Deadline – 23:59 GMT on Monday 5th April 2027.
1) Initial Review: Applications that are poor quality, incomplete or do not meet the essential eligibility criteria or standard will be rejected.
3) Sift Meeting: The experts discuss comments and agree the strongest applications to recommend for funding or inviting to Stage 2. Stage 2 applications then repeat steps 2 and 3.
Funding Decision: Prior to funding being awarded Defra reviews IWTAG’s recommendations, and due diligence checks.

eligibility.quote: Applications must be made by the Lead Organisation, not an individual, agreeing to the Terms and Conditions (see section 3.16) including managing the grant, its finances, reporting and governance. Foreign governments and their agencies cannot be Lead Organisations, though they can be a partner;
Must not be seeking funds with a maximum annual value that exceeds 25% of the Lead Organisation’s average annual turnover/income for the previous 3 years;

IWT Challenge Fund Extra grants, ranging from £600,000 to £1.5 million, are for projects aimed at expanding activities that have a primary focus on addressing IWT, and that have already demonstrated success and impact at a smaller scale (not necessarily funded through the IWT Challenge Fund).
Duration: Projects should last between 2 to 4 years maximum. Projects are required to complete by 31 August 2031.
All schemes require projects to include a poverty reduction focus as this is a core requirement of Official Development Assistance (ODA) funding.

Please note that funding cannot be awarded to organisations or countries that are the target of UK government sanctions. Given the ongoing conflict in Ukraine, the Biodiversity Challenge Funds (BCFs) have taken the decision to suspend all bilateral engagement with Russia. Russian organisations are ineligible to be a Lead Organisation or Partner or involved in any way with BCF grant.

However, applicants cannot make multiple funding applications for the same or similar project in the same year to IWT Challenge Fund, Darwin Plus and/or Ocean Community Empowerment and Nature (OCEAN) Grants Programme.
An unsuccessful application may only be resubmitted once, unless the proposed project is significantly different.

documents.quote: Cover Letter Required (2 sides of A4 maximum). The cover letter supports your application by referring to, rather than duplicating the application.

after_award.quote: Projects must provide Annual and Half Year progress reports that are reviewed each year.
All projects are required to submit a Final Report at the end of the award.
